definition: A security tool or browser extension that prevents potentially harmful or unwanted JavaScript and other scripts from executing on web pages, giving users control over which scripts run.
metaDescription: Learn about script blockers - security tools that prevent unwanted JavaScript from running on websites to protect privacy and improve performance.
simpleExplanation: Think of a script blocker as a bouncer for your web browser. It stops potentially harmful or unwanted code from running on websites you visit, helping protect your privacy and making pages load faster by blocking ads and trackers.
whyItMatters: Script blockers help protect against malicious code, prevent tracking scripts from collecting your data, reduce bandwidth usage, improve page loading speeds, and give you control over your browsing experience.
technicalDetail: Script blockers work by intercepting HTTP requests for JavaScript, Flash, and other executable content before they load. They maintain whitelists and blacklists of allowed/blocked domains, and can selectively enable scripts per site. Popular implementations include NoScript, uBlock Origin, and built-in browser features.

examples.scenario: Visiting a news website with intrusive ads
examples.explanation: A script blocker prevents advertising scripts and trackers from loading, making the page load faster and stopping companies from collecting your browsing data.
The script blocker stops potentially harmful JavaScript from executing, protecting you from drive-by downloads, cryptocurrency miners, or other malicious code.
Script blocking provides an extra layer of security by preventing suspicious scripts from running, even if someone has compromised the network connection.
